sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily, I'm happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Palestine.
Palestine is a small and historic land
in the Middle East.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Palestine?
Palestine is in western Asia, in the Middle East.
It is between Israel, Jordan, and the Mediterranean Sea.
Palestine includes two main areas, the West Bank,
the Gaza Strip.
Some people also call East Jerusalem part of Palestine.
What is the capital city of Palestine?
The capital is considered to be East Jerusalem,
but many government offices are in Ramallah.
Ramallah is a modern city with shops,
cafes, schools, and offices.
Other important cities are Hebron,
Bethlehem, Nablus, Gaza City.
How many people live in Palestine?
About 5 million people live in Palestine.
Some live in cities, others in villages or refugee camps.
Many Palestinians also live in other countries around the world.
Palestinian people are known for their strong culture and hospitality.
What language do people speak in Palestine?
People speak Arabic.
It is the main language in daily life.
Many people also speak English,
especially in schools and tourist areas.
Some people speak Hebrew or French too.
What is the weather like in Palestine?
Palestine has a Mediterranean climate.
This means hot, dry summers,
mild, rainy winters.
In the mountains, winters can be cold.
In Gaza and along the coast, it is warmer.
Spring and autumn are pleasant times to visit.
What does Palestine look like?
Palestine has hills and olive trees,
mountains in the West Bank,
farms and villages,
old cities with stone streets,
the sea along the Gaza coast.
There are also many mosques, churches and markets,
souks.
What animals live in Palestine?
You can find sheep, goats and donkeys,
birds, like doves and owls,
dogs and cats in towns.
In rural areas, foxes, lizards and scorpions.
People raise animals on farms for food and wool.
What do people eat in Palestine?
Palestinian food is fresh and full of flavor.
People eat bread like pita and tabun,
rice, lentils and chickpeas,
vegetables, olive oil and spices.
Popular dishes,
mcluba, rice, meat and vegetables cooked upside down.
Musakan, bread with chicken, onion and sumac,
falafel, fried chickpea balls,
hummus, mashed chickpeas with lemon and tahini.
Stuffed grape leaves called warak and ab.
For dessert, nafah, katayaf, dates and baklava.
What do people drink in Palestine?
People drink tea with mint and sugar,
Arabic coffee with cardamom,
fresh juice like lemon or pomegranate.
Water often served with guests.
Hospitality is very important.
Guests are always offered food or drink.
What is life like in Palestine?
Life can be difficult,
but people are strong and hopeful.
In cities, people go to school, work and markets.
In villages, life is more quiet and traditional.
Family is very important.
People enjoy meals together,
help each other and celebrate special days.
There are also many artists, poets and musicians in Palestine.
What are some holidays and traditions in Palestine?
Eid al-Feter, after Ramadan.
Eid al-Ada, the Feast of Sacrifice.
Christmas, especially in Bethlehem,
the birthplace of Jesus.
Palestinian Land Day, March 30.
Independence Day, November 15.
People wear traditional clothes,
like the Thobe, embroidered dress,
and kafiya, scarf.
There is also traditional Dabke dancing
at weddings and festivals.
Some fun facts about Palestine.
Bethlehem is an important city for Christians.
Olive trees are very important.
Some are over 1,000 years old.
The kafiya scarf is a symbol of Palestinian identity.
Many Palestinians are farmers, teachers, or craftspeople.
The Palestinian flag is black, white, green, and red.
Now you know many things about Palestine.
You know where it is, what people speak,
and what they eat.
You learned about the culture, land, and traditions.
Great job!
Goodbye, or as they say in Arabic,
Ma'a Asalama.
